CONTEXT. This page continues 'Pars 4. Primi formae 8n+7' from the previous page. It is a table, one block per prime p ≡ 7 (mod 8): 151, 167, 191, 199, 223, 239, 263, 271, 311. Each block concerns the properly primitive binary quadratic forms of determinant -p. Since 2 splits when p ≡ 7 mod 8, h(-4p) = h(-p), and h is odd.

HEADER '0.h. 2^(h+2)'. For each prime Gauss records the class number h. All values are correct: h(151)=7, h(167)=11, h(191)=13, h(199)=9, h(223)=7, h(239)=15, h(263)=13, h(271)=11, h(311)=19. The entry 2^(h+2) records that 2^(h+2) is represented by the principal form x^2+py^2 with x, y odd. Equivalently, the h-th power of the class F of the prime form of 2 is principal. My verifications:
- 512 = 19^2 + 151
- 8192 = 3^2 + 167·7^2
- 32768 = 153^2 + 191·7^2
- 2048 = 43^2 + 199
- 512 = 17^2 + 223
- 131072 = 249^2 + 239·17^2
- 32768 = 141^2 + 263·7^2
- 8192 = 89^2 + 271
- For 311, 2^21 = x^2 + 311y^2 is guaranteed by the theory; I did not compute it.

ROWS 'C.i.(h-i) c. 2^(i+2). n1. n2 ...'. The class group is cyclic and generated by F, the class of the determinant -p form representing 8 (equivalently the disc -p form (2,1,(p+1)/8)). Row C.i.(h-i) is the inverse pair F^i, F^-i. In Gauss's determinant convention F^i contains a form (2^(i+2), b, c), hence the entry 2^(i+2). Then follow small odd numbers primitively represented by that pair of classes: split primes, and sometimes composites such as 9, 25, 15, 33. With h odd there are (h+1)/2 rows, matching the previous page's remark 'indicum numerus ... unitate auctus dat bis numerum Classium'.

The parenthesis n(b) distinguishes the two classes of forms (n, b, ...) with b^2 ≡ -p (mod n):
- p=239: -239 ≡ 1 mod 15, so b = 1 or 4.
- p=263: -263 ≡ 1 mod 33, so b = 1.
- p=311: -311 ≡ 4 mod 15, so b = 2.

MY VERIFICATION BY COMPOSITION (disc -p reduced forms, repeated composition with f = (2,1,(p+1)/8)):
- 167: f^2=(4,-3,11) gives 11; f^3=(6,-5,8); f^4=(3,1,14) gives 3; f^5=(6,1,7) gives 7.
- 191: f^2=(4,1,12) gives 17 at (1,1); f^3=(6,-1,8) gives 13; f^4=(3,-1,16) gives 3; f^5=(6,5,9); f^6=(5,-3,10) gives 5.
- 199: f=(2,1,25) gives 31 at (-2,1); f^2=(4,-3,13); f^3=(7,-5,8); f^4=(5,1,10).
- 223: f gives 29; f^2=(4,1,14) gives 17; f^3=(7,-1,8).
- 239: f gives 31; f^2=(4,1,15) is the class of 15(1); f^3=(8,-7,9) gives 9; f^4=(5,1,12); f^5=(6,-1,10) is the class of 15(4) and also gives 17.
- 263: f=(2,1,33) gives 33; f^2=(4,-3,17); f^3=(8,5,9); f^4=(16,21,11) gives 11; f^5=(3,-1,22); f^6=(6,5,12) gives 13.
- 271: f^2=(4,1,17); f^3=(8,9,11); f^4=(5,-3,14); f^5=(7,3,10).
- 311: f^3=(8,-3,10) gives 15; f^4=(5,3,16); f^5=(9,7,10); f^6=(6,-1,13); f^7=(3,-1,26); f^8=(6,5,14) gives 25; f^10=(7,5,12) gives 7.

For 151 only the class pairs are listed, with no representatives. All recorded assignments agree with these computations.

PURPOSE. This is an empirical tabulation of the cyclic class-group structure for prime negative determinants. It shows the class of the prime form of 2 as generator, its period length h, and which small primes fall in which power class. It belongs to Gauss's class-number and period investigations (cf. Disquisitiones Arithmeticae arts. 305-307 and the class-number tables in Werke II).
errors: 223: Gauss first wrote an extra row 'C.4.7 c:2^6', which is impossible for h=7 because the pairs are 0, 1·6, 2·5, 3·4. He struck it out himself; it is not an error in the final table.

311, row C.3.16: the reading '16(2)' cannot be right. Forms (16,b,..) of determinant -311 would need b^2 ≡ 9 (mod 16), so b ≠ 2. The intended entry is 15(2): -311 ≡ 4 (mod 15), and 15 is represented by f^3 = (8,-3,10). The same notation 15(2) appears on the next page for 431. This is either an overwritten digit or a slip.
151: no represented numbers are given; the block is incomplete rather than wrong.
No mathematical errors found in the class numbers, the 2^(h+2) entries, or the class assignments I checked.
Next page, not this one: headers '2^11' for 359 and '2^9' for 383, 431, 503 are inconsistent with the 2^(h+2) pattern (they should be 2^21, 2^19, 2^23, 2^23). This is a slip or a transcription issue.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful empirical table of class numbers and cyclic class-group structure for prime determinants -p, p ≡ 7 mod 8, generated by the prime form of 2. Such tabulations are well known as Gauss's work (DA arts. 305-307; class-number tables in Werke II). The specific data are a correct, moderately interesting unpublished detail, but nothing beyond Gauss's known methods.
